title: Family sues cop for son's death: [FINAL C Edition]
article: A police officer is being sued after shooting to death a machete- wielding teen in Port Moody.
"The police can use deadly force only when there is no alternative," said Don Morrison, a lawyer representing the family of Keyvan Tabesh.
The Port Moody police officer, a former Mountie, coach and youth liaison officer, killed Iranian-born Tabesh, 18, on July 14, 2003.

The officer, who has yet to be named, was responding to a 911 call after Tabesh allegedly chased a vehicle carrying two women then got out of his car and smashed in their window with a machete. Tabesh was suspended from driving at the time.
The officer followed Tabesh's vehicle into a dead-end street. Tabesh got out, wielding the machete, and approa-ched the officer.
The officer, who was in an unmarked vehicle and not in uniform, shot Tabesh five times when he didn't drop the mach-ete. In June 2004, the attorney-general chose not to charge the officer.
The B.C. Coroner's Service is to hold an inquest into Tabesh's death next month.
